check: Raw Sleep-EDFx download at F:/sleep edf signals
prompted_by: a question about which dataset to attach, which made it worth checking whether the local mirror was complete at all

finding.problem: ST7102J0-PSG.edf was listed in RECORDS but absent from disk. Its HYPNOGRAM (ST7102JE-Hypnogram.edf) was present, so nothing looked obviously broken: 196 PSG files against 197 hypnograms.
finding.cause: an incomplete wget mirror dropped one signal file
finding.why_it_was_nearly_invisible: A recording whose PSG never downloaded is not 'skipped' by the preprocessor - it is never seen, so it cannot appear in the skip list and the run reports complete success. The only symptom was a tensor count of 196 against the 197 the original pipeline produced.
finding.severity: ST710 is in the TEST split. A model trained and evaluated on the short set would have had 28 test recordings against the 29 every published number uses - silently incomparable, with no error.

not_affected.why: processed_sleepedf (the original single-channel tensors) already contained all 197 recordings, including a valid 980-epoch ST7102J0 consistent with its index entry. That set was built from a complete download. Only this local raw-EDF mirror was short, and only the new multi-channel preprocessing consumed it.

guard_added: preprocess_multichannel.py now checks the produced recording set against splits.json and exits non-zero listing what is missing and which split it belongs to. Counting outputs was not enough - the produced set has to be compared against the set the splits expect.
